prohibited_concomitant: topicals except mild/low-potency topical steroids for face, axilla, genitalia
anti-TNF biologics (etanercept, infliximab, golimumab, certolizumab pegol, adalimumab)
permitted_concomitant: topical moisturizers/emollients, bath oils, oatmeal bath preparations as needed
mild and low-potency topical steroids limited to face, axilla, and/or genitalia, as needed (not within ~24 hours of IGA/PASI visits)

mild pain relievers (acetaminophen/paracetamol, mild opiates) for arthritis pain
intra-articular steroid or hyaluronic acid injections after Week 16
value.population_note: This is a psoriasis biologic/active-comparator trial (bimekizumab vs. ustekinumab vs. placebo), not an AD/TCS-flavored design, so regimen_type does not map to any of the 3 enum values (monotherapy doesn't strictly apply since limited topical corticosteroid use on face/axilla/genitalia is explicitly permitted, not prohibited). Left null as a real schema-enum gap; the permitted/prohibited concomitant lists below are the actual protocol Section 7.8 policy.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 7.8.1.1 Topical medications: "Subjects may continue to use topical moisturizers or emollients, bath oils, or oatmeal bath preparations for skin conditions during the study, as needed... Mild and low potency topical steroids will be permitted for use limited to the face, axilla, and/or genitalia, as needed." Section 7.8.2, Table 7-2 Prohibited psoriasis medications: lists topicals (except permitted), systemic retinoids, systemic immunosuppressants, fumaric acid esters, systemic corticosteroids, phototherapy, anti-TNFs, ustekinumab, apremilast/tofacitinib, alefacept/efalizumab/guselkumab, tildrakizumab/risankizumab, briakinumab, rituximab, and anti-IL-17 therapy (secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab), each with a stated washout period.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: SAP Section 4.5 Multiple comparisons/multiplicity: "The statistical analysis of the co-primary efficacy variables and selected secondary efficacy variables will account for multiplicity and control the familywise Type I error rate at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05 by using a fixed sequence testing procedure... The first 2 hypotheses (H1 and H2) test whether bimekizumab is superior to placebo for PASI90 response and IGA response at Week 16... If both are rejected at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05, that alpha will be passed to the next test in the sequence, allowing the testing procedure to proceed."

maintenance_arms: placebo subjects switched to bimekizumab 320mg Q4W at Week 16
value.source_inconsistency: An earlier protocol amendment (superseded, visible in this document's tracked-changes appendix) included a Week-16 PASI90-triggered 'escape arm' to bimekizumab plus a mandatory Week-28+ PASI50 withdrawal rule; the final approved Section 5 Study Design (used here) removed the escape arm and instead switches ALL placebo subjects unconditionally to bimekizumab 320mg Q4W at the start of the Maintenance Treatment Period (Week 16), with no PASI50-based mandatory withdrawal rule stated in the final design.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Section 5.2 Study periods: "This study will include 4 periods, a Screening Period (2 to 5 weeks), an Initial Treatment Period (16 weeks), a Maintenance Treatment Period (36 weeks), and a SFU Period (20 weeks after the final dose of IMP)." Section 5.2.3: "Subjects in the placebo arm will receive bimekizumab 320mg Q4W" during Maintenance. Section 5.3: "For each subject, the study will last a maximum of up to 73 weeks."
